title: I'm done using AI
excerpt: Why I'm stopping using AI for coding (and anything else) after using it earnestly for a year and coming to understand the harms it causes on personal, societal, and environmental levels.
content_html:
10 Aug, 2026

I've been programming for 20 years. It started as a hobby as a teen, making fansites and little video games. Then it turned into a career. And it's something I've largely enjoyed doing. I like learning, I like problem solving, and I like making things, which is a lot of what programming is. Over the past 18 months, my career, my hobby, and my craft have been drastically changed by the introduction of LLM-powered coding harnesses (e.g., Claude Code) and what's often referred to as "agentic programming." Because of its negative impacts on the environment, society, and my mental health, I've decided to stop using it.

▶ Watch a ramble video version of this post.

I first became aware of using LLMs for programming a few years ago through GitHub's Copilot integration in Visual Studio Code, which was like autocomplete on steroids. You'd start typing function sortNames and it'd show you a preview of what that implementation could look like. I tried it and found it distracting and basically useless. The second time it reared its head was the early chat interfaces. A colleague was using it to help investigate an issue and the solution the LLM provided them with wasn't working. Turns out that the LLM hallucinated a version of a software library that didn't exist, and therefore couldn't be installed nor used to fix the issue.

Around this time, at that job, a true believer of AI was hired as the head of the product team. They were a product manager who began submitting changes, using the LLM-powered coding tools but without understanding the implications to the broader system. Conversations became focused on how to integrate AI into the software that the customers used. I was watching it spread like a virus throughout that organization, while I continued programming away as I had for the decades before, writing tests and building features, and largely enjoying the work.

At a newer job, the job I have now as I write this, I continued to code how I had my entire life. Writing TypeScript, Ruby, CSS, etc. and corresponding tests, integrating with other systems and depdnencies. It's a small team of less than 10 developers. On collaborative calls, I'd see how some of my colleagues utilized AI in the Cursor editor, quickly tab completing the code and sometimes prompting it inline to write some code. The LLM-powered coding tooling at that time was largely working at a local-to-that-file, small scale. I thought it was neat, almost magical, but nothing would pry me away from Neovim and tmux, and I felt like I was working fast enough anyway.

I didn't, and I still don't, see the need for working faster. I really like what Cal Newport encourages in his book Slow Productivity: work at a natural pace.

In early 2025 I was asked a question by management: "what do you think of this AI coding stuff?" And I said "it's often wrong, gets in my way, and doesn't help me code faster, so I don't use it." Management would not long after attend a conference and be sold on how LLMs would change everything we know about knowledge work, revolutionizing the workplace. This then led to a mandate to make use of AI tools or be left behind.

I decided to give AI a go, in earnest. I tried the Cursor editor, but it didn't click with me and ran horribly on Linux. So I tried Zed, and pretty soon thereafter I was utilizing the sidebar chat with auto-edit to have the LLMs make changes to the code and build software. At that time, it honestly felt magical. Type into a box and the thing would write code and answer my questions. During mid-2025, agentic editing became the new way to use AI for coding, replacing the auto-complete-based workflows. As the AI companies invested in training models tuned for that purpose and building coding harnesses, the capabilities kept getting better and better.

Fast forward a year to mid-2026. In the lead up to my decision to stop using AI, I was able to essentially connect Linear to Claude Code and have it build out a non-trivial project from start to finish without me editing a line of code. The work got done faster than I could have done on my own. And I barely had to think. While that sounds amazing if you're a person who profits from more work getting done, there are immense drawbacks to this, which I'll share more about in a moment. I share this anecdote to say: I understand what the LLM-based coding harnesses are capable of. I write this all from the perspective of an experienced lead engineer who used these tools in earnest for more than a year. And I cannot in good conscious continue to use AI for coding (or anything else) any longer.

During the time when I started using the LLM coding tools, I also started to use the chat functionality. I'd ask it to recommend me books. I'd ask for career advice. I'd float business ideas by it. I talked to it like it was a friend. I'd come up with grand ideas, and it was always supportive. And I'd ask it for medical advice. I'm embarrassed to admit this, but one night when I was sick, I described all my symptoms and it told me to go to the Emergency Department at the hospital. So I hopped in my car at midnight, suffering from the flu, and drove to the ED. I sat there and waited for two hours in the waiting room while my ibuprofen I took before I left kicked in. By the time I saw a medical professional, they basically just told me to go home and rest, that I didn't need to go to the ED. While sure, yeah, better safe than sorry can sometimes apply to the ED, I think relying on the AI chat for what action to take for my medical condition was a huge mistake. It also cost me hundreds of dollars. That example, among others, helped me realize the AI chat was making me delusional.

I stopped using the AI chat because it became very clear it wasn't helpful or healthy, and it was in fact dangerous. But I kept using AI for coding at work, using it to take on more and more of the heavy-lifting to the point where I was just a code reviewer and a quality assurance tester for the features the coding harness would spit out. Getting a lot of tasks done, it can feel exhilarating. That is, until I realized, well, I'm basically just a hamster on a wheel, checking boxes, getting tickets done with no real purpose. Sure, I catch an issue here or there. But it's impossible to review the quantity of code the AI writes, and we've got a different AI to review it anyway! So what did this do? Well, it made me lazy. It made me stop caring. It made me a worse programmer. It made me depressed. Because I stopped doing the hard work, I stopped learning, I stopped growing, I stopped being the one making the software.

I had a conversation with management about how a developer's job is now is to teach the AI to be better, make fewer mistakes, etc. To review the code. And to test the changes that the AI makes. This is a horrible existence, and it was one of the other signs that this is untenable for me to continue like this.

One of the other signs that something had to change is that the more I used AI for coding at work, the more distant I felt from the software and its features. I couldn't explain precisely how something worked without asking the AI. I cared far less about the code and the software itself because I didn't write any of that code myself, I was removed from it.

Upon reflection, I've come to believe that quality software is not about how many features something has or how quickly it is built but rather how cared for it is by the designers, developers, and product people who work on it. There's an ineffable aspect to my favorite pieces of software where I don't think of it is as feature matrix but rather as an interface made by a human for humans that's a joy to use. And when you build software with AI, it leads to worse software. Sure, it's faster to build initially, but I think to the detriment of the quality of the code and the user interface and the user experience.

I also started experiencing existential dread. If I'm basically just feeding Linear tickets into a CLI, why am I needed at all? Will software engineering exist in a few years? Should I go become an electrician or something else entirely? But what about this craft I love and career I've had? Will it just go away?

I started to learn more about the true cost of AI, from the data centers to the water usage and beyond. That it's built and trained upon stolen sources. And the cost is extreme. And that cost is largely hidden from people unless they're building a data center in your backyard (which they might be before you know it).

So in summary: using AI for coding led to depression, apathy, existential dread, and worse software. Not good. Add on top of that the negative environmental, community, and economic impacts of AI, and it became extremely apparent to me that something's gotta change.

Earlier in the year, at the nadir of all of this, I returned to one of my hobbies: game programming. During this time, I finished writing my book on coding games for Playdate, made some small games, and created a 2D Lua game engine called Usagi with Rust. I was feeling disillusioned with coding at work and going back to the basics by writing and coding without AI helped me realize how much I love coding and how using AI was making me a worse programmer and negatively impacting my mental state.

I tried to use AI less at work, like only use it for trivial tasks, but that never really worked. I'd just fall back to using it for pretty much everything. It feels silly to type out a test when you can just have AI do all of it. For me, it feels like an all or nothing decision. Also, using it less but still using it means I'd still be using it, therefore showing demand for it and contributing to the harms it causes. No thanks.

When someone decides to make use of some technology, or more abstractly a tool, there's always some sort of cost to using it. The cost of using LLM-based tooling is way too high and absolutely not worth it, in my opinion, for myself or society. In my opinion, AI is unquestionably a net harm compared to any benefits it may provide.

To put it simply: I do not like this world where people are using AI to generate art, music, writing, and software. So I will not use AI.

I don't know what consequences will come from this decision to stop using AI for coding at work. It is possible I will be terminated. It's possible I'll be able to get by just fine. Time will tell. But all I know is that I couldn't keep working that way, as it was in no uncertain terms ruining my life.

What comes next, I'm not quite certain. I want to talk about all this more. I want to see how other developers are fairing. I want to return to my love of sharing what I learn and helping other programmers through writing and videos. Well, helping those who want to actually learn to program, not those that want to just prompt their way to a solution. It's a strange and uncertain time, that's for sure. But I'm going to see what the future brings and stick to my values and be true to myself. Here's to writing code by hand.

#anti-ai #personal

sentences.en: And I said "it's often wrong, gets in my way, and doesn't help me code faster, so I don't use it."
sentences.zh: 我说“它经常是错误的，妨碍我，并且不能帮助我更快地编码，所以我不使用它。”

sentences.en: Management would not long after attend a conference and be sold on how LLMs would change everything we know about knowledge work, revolutionizing the workplace.
sentences.zh: 管理层在参加一次会议后不久就会相信法学硕士将如何改变我们对知识工作的了解，彻底改变工作场所。

sentences.en: This then led to a mandate to make use of AI tools or be left behind.
sentences.zh: 这导致了使用人工智能工具的强制要求，否则就会被抛在后面。

blocks.html_en: I decided to give AI a go, in earnest. I tried the Cursor editor, but it didn't click with me and ran horribly on Linux. So I tried Zed, and pretty soon thereafter I was utilizing the sidebar chat with auto-edit to have the LLMs make changes to the code and build software. At that time, it honestly felt magical. Type into a box and the thing would write code and answer my questions. During mid-2025, agentic editing became the new way to use AI for coding, replacing the auto-complete-based workflows. As the AI companies invested in training models tuned for that purpose and building coding harnesses, the capabilities kept getting better and better.

sentences.en: I decided to give AI a go, in earnest.
sentences.zh: 我决定认真地尝试一下人工智能。

sentences.en: I tried the Cursor editor, but it didn't click with me and ran horribly on Linux.
sentences.zh: 我尝试了光标编辑器，但它不适合我，并且在 Linux 上运行得很糟糕。

sentences.en: So I tried Zed, and pretty soon thereafter I was utilizing the sidebar chat with auto-edit to have the LLMs make changes to the code and build software.
sentences.zh: 所以我尝试了 Zed，不久之后我就利用带有自动编辑功能的侧边栏聊天让法学硕士更改代码并构建软件。

sentences.en: At that time, it honestly felt magical.
sentences.zh: 当时真的感觉很神奇。

sentences.en: Type into a box and the thing would write code and answer my questions.
sentences.zh: 在一个框中输入内容，它就会编写代码并回答我的问题。

sentences.en: During mid-2025, agentic editing became the new way to use AI for coding, replacing the auto-complete-based workflows.
sentences.zh: 2025 年中期，代理编辑成为使用 AI 进行编码的新方式，取代了基于自动完成的工作流程。

sentences.en: As the AI companies invested in training models tuned for that purpose and building coding harnesses, the capabilities kept getting better and better.
sentences.zh: 随着人工智能公司投资为此目的调整的培训模型并构建编码工具，其功能不断变得越来越好。

blocks.html_en: Fast forward a year to mid-2026. In the lead up to my decision to stop using AI, I was able to essentially connect Linear to Claude Code and have it build out a non-trivial project from start to finish without me editing a line of code. The work got done faster than I could have done on my own. And I barely had to think. While that sounds amazing if you're a person who profits from more work getting done, there are immense drawbacks to this, which I'll share more about in a moment. I share this anecdote to say: I understand what the LLM-based coding harnesses are capable of. I write this all from the perspective of an experienced lead engineer who used these tools in earnest for more than a year. And I cannot in good conscious continue to use AI for coding (or anything else) any longer.

sentences.en: Fast forward a year to mid-2026.
sentences.zh: 快进一年到 2026 年中期。

sentences.en: In the lead up to my decision to stop using AI, I was able to essentially connect Linear to Claude Code and have it build out a non-trivial project from start to finish without me editing a line of code.
sentences.zh: 在我决定停止使用人工智能之前，我基本上能够将 Linear 与 Claude Code 连接起来，并让它从头到尾构建一个不平凡的项目，而无需我编辑一行代码。

sentences.en: The work got done faster than I could have done on my own.
sentences.zh: 这项工作完成得比我自己更快。

sentences.en: And I barely had to think.
sentences.zh: 我几乎不需要思考。

sentences.en: While that sounds amazing if you're a person who profits from more work getting done, there are immense drawbacks to this, which I'll share more about in a moment.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个从完成更多工作中获益的人，这听起来很神奇，但这样做也有巨大的缺点，我稍后会详细分享。

sentences.en: I share this anecdote to say: I understand what the LLM-based coding harnesses are capable of.
sentences.zh: 我分享这个轶事是为了说：我了解基于 LLM 的编码工具的能力。

sentences.en: I write this all from the perspective of an experienced lead engineer who used these tools in earnest for more than a year.
sentences.zh: 我是从一位经验丰富的首席工程师的角度写下这一切的，他认真使用了这些工具一年多了。

sentences.en: And I cannot in good conscious continue to use AI for coding (or anything else) any longer.
sentences.zh: 我不能再有意识地继续使用人工智能进行编码（或其他任何事情）。

blocks.html_en: During the time when I started using the LLM coding tools, I also started to use the chat functionality. I'd ask it to recommend me books. I'd ask for career advice. I'd float business ideas by it. I talked to it like it was a friend. I'd come up with grand ideas, and it was always supportive. And I'd ask it for medical advice. I'm embarrassed to admit this, but one night when I was sick, I described all my symptoms and it told me to go to the Emergency Department at the hospital. So I hopped in my car at midnight, suffering from the flu, and drove to the ED. I sat there and waited for two hours in the waiting room while my ibuprofen I took before I left kicked in. By the time I saw a medical professional, they basically just told me to go home and rest, that I didn't need to go to the ED. While sure, yeah, better safe than sorry can sometimes apply to the ED, I think relying on the AI chat for what action to take for my medical condition was a huge mistake. It also cost me hundreds of dollars. That example, among others, helped me realize the AI chat was making me delusional.

sentences.en: During the time when I started using the LLM coding tools, I also started to use the chat functionality.
sentences.zh: 在我开始使用LLM编码工具的同时，我也开始使用聊天功能。

sentences.en: I'd ask it to recommend me books.
sentences.zh: 我会要求它给我推荐书籍。

sentences.en: I'd ask for career advice.
sentences.zh: 我会寻求职业建议。

sentences.en: I'd float business ideas by it.
sentences.zh: 我会通过它来表达商业想法。

sentences.en: I talked to it like it was a friend.
sentences.zh: 我像朋友一样和它交谈。

sentences.en: I'd come up with grand ideas, and it was always supportive.
sentences.zh: 我提出了宏伟的想法，并且总是得到支持。

sentences.en: And I'd ask it for medical advice.
sentences.zh: 我会向它寻求医疗建议。

sentences.en: I'm embarrassed to admit this, but one night when I was sick, I described all my symptoms and it told me to go to the Emergency Department at the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我不好意思承认这一点，但有一天晚上，当我生病时，我描述了我所有的症状，它告诉我去医院的急诊室。

sentences.en: So I hopped in my car at midnight, suffering from the flu, and drove to the ED.
sentences.zh: 于是我在半夜跳上车，患上了流感，开车去了急诊室。

sentences.en: I sat there and waited for two hours in the waiting room while my ibuprofen I took before I left kicked in.
sentences.zh: 我坐在候诊室里等了两个小时，离开前服用的布洛芬开始发挥作用。

sentences.en: By the time I saw a medical professional, they basically just told me to go home and rest, that I didn't need to go to the ED.
sentences.zh: 当我去看医生时，他们基本上只是告诉我回家休息，不需要去急诊室。

sentences.en: While sure, yeah, better safe than sorry can sometimes apply to the ED, I think relying on the AI chat for what action to take for my medical condition was a huge mistake.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的，安全总比后悔有时适用于急诊室，但我认为依靠人工智能聊天来针对我的医疗状况采取什么行动是一个巨大的错误。

sentences.en: It also cost me hundreds of dollars.
sentences.zh: 我也花了几百美元。

sentences.en: That example, among others, helped me realize the AI chat was making me delusional.
sentences.zh: 这个例子让我意识到人工智能聊天让我产生了妄想。

blocks.html_en: I stopped using the AI chat because it became very clear it wasn't helpful or healthy, and it was in fact dangerous. But I kept using AI for coding at work, using it to take on more and more of the heavy-lifting to the point where I was just a code reviewer and a quality assurance tester for the features the coding harness would spit out. Getting a lot of tasks done, it can feel exhilarating. That is, until I realized, well, I'm basically just a hamster on a wheel, checking boxes, getting tickets done with no real purpose. Sure, I catch an issue here or there. But it's impossible to review the quantity of code the AI writes, and we've got a different AI to review it anyway! So what did this do? Well, it made me lazy. It made me stop caring. It made me a worse programmer. It made me depressed. Because I stopped doing the hard work, I stopped learning, I stopped growing, I stopped being the one making the software.

sentences.en: I stopped using the AI chat because it became very clear it wasn't helpful or healthy, and it was in fact dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我停止使用人工智能聊天，因为很明显它没有帮助或不健康，而且实际上很危险。

sentences.en: But I kept using AI for coding at work, using it to take on more and more of the heavy-lifting to the point where I was just a code reviewer and a quality assurance tester for the features the coding harness would spit out.
sentences.zh: 但我在工作中一直使用人工智能进行编码，用它来承担越来越多的繁重工作，以至于我只是一名代码审查员和编码工具所吐出的功能的质量保证测试员。

sentences.en: Getting a lot of tasks done, it can feel exhilarating.
sentences.zh: 完成很多任务，会让人感到兴奋。

sentences.en: That is, until I realized, well, I'm basically just a hamster on a wheel, checking boxes, getting tickets done with no real purpose.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，直到我意识到，好吧，我基本上只是一只轮子上的仓鼠，检查箱子，毫无意义地完成门票。

sentences.en: Sure, I catch an issue here or there.
sentences.zh: 当然，我在这里或那里发现了一个问题。

sentences.en: But it's impossible to review the quantity of code the AI writes, and we've got a different AI to review it anyway!
sentences.zh: 但不可能审查人工智能编写的代码数量，而且无论如何我们都有不同的人工智能来审查它！

sentences.en: So what did this do?
sentences.zh: 那么这是做什么的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it made me lazy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这让我变得懒惰了。

sentences.en: It made me stop caring.
sentences.zh: 这让我不再关心。

sentences.en: It made me a worse programmer.
sentences.zh: 这让我成为了一个更糟糕的程序员。

sentences.en: It made me depressed.
sentences.zh: 这让我很沮丧。

sentences.en: Because I stopped doing the hard work, I stopped learning, I stopped growing, I stopped being the one making the software.
sentences.zh: 因为我停止了艰苦的工作，我停止了学习，我停止了成长，我不再是软件的制作者。

blocks.html_en: I had a conversation with management about how a developer's job is now is to teach the AI to be better, make fewer mistakes, etc. To review the code. And to test the changes that the AI makes. This is a horrible existence, and it was one of the other signs that this is untenable for me to continue like this.

sentences.en: I had a conversation with management about how a developer's job is now is to teach the AI to be better, make fewer mistakes, etc. To review the code.
sentences.zh: 我与管理层进行了一次对话，讨论开发人员现在的工作是教人工智能变得更好，减少错误等等。审查代码。

sentences.en: And to test the changes that the AI makes.
sentences.zh: 并测试人工智能所做的改变。

sentences.en: This is a horrible existence, and it was one of the other signs that this is untenable for me to continue like this.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可怕的存在，这是我无法继续这样下去的其他迹象之一。

blocks.html_en: One of the other signs that something had to change is that the more I used AI for coding at work, the more distant I felt from the software and its features. I couldn't explain precisely how something worked without asking the AI. I cared far less about the code and the software itself because I didn't write any of that code myself, I was removed from it.

sentences.en: One of the other signs that something had to change is that the more I used AI for coding at work, the more distant I felt from the software and its features.
sentences.zh: 必须做出改变的其他迹象之一是，我在工作中使用人工智能进行编码的次数越多，我对软件及其功能的感觉就越遥远。

sentences.en: I couldn't explain precisely how something worked without asking the AI.
sentences.zh: 如果不询问人工智能，我就无法准确解释某些东西是如何工作的。

sentences.en: I cared far less about the code and the software itself because I didn't write any of that code myself, I was removed from it.
sentences.zh: 我不太关心代码和软件本身，因为我自己没有编写任何代码，我被从其中删除了。

blocks.html_en: Upon reflection, I've come to believe that quality software is not about how many features something has or how quickly it is built but rather how cared for it is by the designers, developers, and product people who work on it. There's an ineffable aspect to my favorite pieces of software where I don't think of it is as feature matrix but rather as an interface made by a human for humans that's a joy to use. And when you build software with AI, it leads to worse software. Sure, it's faster to build initially, but I think to the detriment of the quality of the code and the user interface and the user experience.

sentences.en: Upon reflection, I've come to believe that quality software is not about how many features something has or how quickly it is built but rather how cared for it is by the designers, developers, and product people who work on it.
sentences.zh: 经过反思，我开始相信，高质量的软件并不在于某个东西有多少功能或者它的构建速度有多快，而是在于设计者、开发者和产品人员对其工作的关心程度。

sentences.en: There's an ineffable aspect to my favorite pieces of software where I don't think of it is as feature matrix but rather as an interface made by a human for humans that's a joy to use.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的软件有一个难以形容的方面，我不认为它是一个功能矩阵，而是一个由人类为人类制作的界面，使用起来很有趣。

sentences.en: And when you build software with AI, it leads to worse software.
sentences.zh: 当你用人工智能构建软件时，它会导致更糟糕的软件。

sentences.en: Sure, it's faster to build initially, but I think to the detriment of the quality of the code and the user interface and the user experience.
sentences.zh: 当然，最初构建速度更快，但我认为这会损害代码质量、用户界面和用户体验。

blocks.html_en: I also started experiencing existential dread. If I'm basically just feeding Linear tickets into a CLI, why am I needed at all? Will software engineering exist in a few years? Should I go become an electrician or something else entirely? But what about this craft I love and career I've had? Will it just go away?

sentences.en: I also started experiencing existential dread.
sentences.zh: 我也开始经历存在主义的恐惧。

sentences.en: If I'm basically just feeding Linear tickets into a CLI, why am I needed at all?
sentences.zh: 如果我基本上只是将 Linear 票证输入 CLI，那为什么还需要我呢？

sentences.en: Will software engineering exist in a few years?
sentences.zh: 几年后软件工程还会存在吗？

sentences.en: Should I go become an electrician or something else entirely?
sentences.zh: 我应该成为一名电工还是其他职业？

sentences.en: But what about this craft I love and career I've had?
sentences.zh: 但我所热爱的这门手艺和我所拥有的职业又如何呢？

sentences.en: Will it just go away?
sentences.zh: 它会消失吗？

blocks.html_en: I started to learn more about the true cost of AI, from the data centers to the water usage and beyond. That it's built and trained upon stolen sources. And the cost is extreme. And that cost is largely hidden from people unless they're building a data center in your backyard (which they might be before you know it).

sentences.en: I started to learn more about the true cost of AI, from the data centers to the water usage and beyond.
sentences.zh: 我开始更多地了解人工智能的真正成本，从数据中心到用水等等。

sentences.en: That it's built and trained upon stolen sources.
sentences.zh: 它是在窃取的资源上构建和训练的。

sentences.en: And the cost is extreme.
sentences.zh: 而且成本是极端的。

sentences.en: And that cost is largely hidden from people unless they're building a data center in your backyard (which they might be before you know it).
sentences.zh: 除非他们在您的后院建立数据中心（在您意识到之前他们可能就在您的后院），否则这种成本在很大程度上是对人们隐藏的。

blocks.html_en: So in summary: using AI for coding led to depression, apathy, existential dread, and worse software. Not good. Add on top of that the negative environmental, community, and economic impacts of AI, and it became extremely apparent to me that something's gotta change.

sentences.en: So in summary: using AI for coding led to depression, apathy, existential dread, and worse software.
sentences.zh: 总而言之：使用人工智能进行编码会导致抑郁、冷漠、生存恐惧和更糟糕的软件。

sentences.en: Not good.
sentences.zh: 不好。

sentences.en: Add on top of that the negative environmental, community, and economic impacts of AI, and it became extremely apparent to me that something's gotta change.
sentences.zh: 再加上人工智能对环境、社区和经济的负面影响，对我来说，很明显有些事情必须改变。

blocks.html_en: Earlier in the year, at the nadir of all of this, I returned to one of my hobbies: game programming. During this time, I finished writing my book on coding games for Playdate, made some small games, and created a 2D Lua game engine called Usagi with Rust. I was feeling disillusioned with coding at work and going back to the basics by writing and coding without AI helped me realize how much I love coding and how using AI was making me a worse programmer and negatively impacting my mental state.

sentences.en: Earlier in the year, at the nadir of all of this, I returned to one of my hobbies: game programming.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，在这一切的最低谷时，我又回到了我的爱好之一：游戏编程。

sentences.en: During this time, I finished writing my book on coding games for Playdate, made some small games, and created a 2D Lua game engine called Usagi with Rust.
sentences.zh: 这段时间，我为 Playdate 写完了关于游戏编码的书，制作了一些小游戏，并用 Rust 创建了一个名为 Usagi 的 2D Lua 游戏引擎。

sentences.en: I was feeling disillusioned with coding at work and going back to the basics by writing and coding without AI helped me realize how much I love coding and how using AI was making me a worse programmer and negatively impacting my mental state.
sentences.zh: 我对工作中的编码感到幻灭，在没有人工智能的情况下通过编写和编码回到基础知识帮助我意识到我有多么喜欢编码以及使用人工智能如何使我成为一个更糟糕的程序员并对我的精神状态产生负面影响。

blocks.html_en: I tried to use AI less at work, like only use it for trivial tasks, but that never really worked. I'd just fall back to using it for pretty much everything. It feels silly to type out a test when you can just have AI do all of it. For me, it feels like an all or nothing decision. Also, using it less but still using it means I'd still be using it, therefore showing demand for it and contributing to the harms it causes. No thanks.

sentences.en: I tried to use AI less at work, like only use it for trivial tasks, but that never really worked.
sentences.zh: 我尝试在工作中减少人工智能的使用，比如只将其用于琐碎的任务，但这从未真正奏效。

sentences.en: I'd just fall back to using it for pretty much everything.
sentences.zh: 我会重新使用它来完成几乎所有事情。

sentences.en: It feels silly to type out a test when you can just have AI do all of it.
sentences.zh: 当你可以让人工智能完成所有的事情时，编写一个测试感觉很愚蠢。

sentences.en: For me, it feels like an all or nothing decision.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这感觉像是一个全有或全无的决定。

sentences.en: Also, using it less but still using it means I'd still be using it, therefore showing demand for it and contributing to the harms it causes.
sentences.zh: 此外，减少使用它但仍然使用它意味着我仍然会使用它，因此显示出对它的需求并加剧了它造成的危害。

sentences.en: No thanks.
sentences.zh: 不，谢谢。

blocks.html_en: When someone decides to make use of some technology, or more abstractly a tool, there's always some sort of cost to using it. The cost of using LLM-based tooling is way too high and absolutely not worth it, in my opinion, for myself or society. In my opinion, AI is unquestionably a net harm compared to any benefits it may provide.

sentences.en: When someone decides to make use of some technology, or more abstractly a tool, there's always some sort of cost to using it.
sentences.zh: 当有人决定使用某种技术，或者更抽象地说是一种工具时，使用它总是会产生某种成本。

sentences.en: The cost of using LLM-based tooling is way too high and absolutely not worth it, in my opinion, for myself or society.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，使用基于法学硕士的工具的成本太高，对于我自己或社会来说绝对不值得。

sentences.en: In my opinion, AI is unquestionably a net harm compared to any benefits it may provide.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，与人工智能可能提供的任何好处相比，人工智能无疑是一种净危害。

blocks.html_en: To put it simply: I do not like this world where people are using AI to generate art, music, writing, and software. So I will not use AI.

sentences.en: To put it simply: I do not like this world where people are using AI to generate art, music, writing, and software.
sentences.zh: 简而言之：我不喜欢这个人们使用人工智能来生成艺术、音乐、写作和软件的世界。

sentences.en: So I will not use AI.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会使用AI。

blocks.html_en: I don't know what consequences will come from this decision to stop using AI for coding at work. It is possible I will be terminated. It's possible I'll be able to get by just fine. Time will tell. But all I know is that I couldn't keep working that way, as it was in no uncertain terms ruining my life.

sentences.en: I don't know what consequences will come from this decision to stop using AI for coding at work.
sentences.zh: 我不知道停止在工作中使用人工智能进行编码的决定会产生什么后果。

sentences.en: It is possible I will be terminated.
sentences.zh: 我可能会被解雇。

sentences.en: It's possible I'll be able to get by just fine.
sentences.zh: 或许我能过得很好。

sentences.en: Time will tell.
sentences.zh: 时间会证明一切。

sentences.en: But all I know is that I couldn't keep working that way, as it was in no uncertain terms ruining my life.
sentences.zh: 但我只知道我不能继续这样工作，因为这无疑会毁掉我的生活。

blocks.html_en: What comes next, I'm not quite certain. I want to talk about all this more. I want to see how other developers are fairing. I want to return to my love of sharing what I learn and helping other programmers through writing and videos. Well, helping those who want to actually learn to program, not those that want to just prompt their way to a solution. It's a strange and uncertain time, that's for sure. But I'm going to see what the future brings and stick to my values and be true to myself. Here's to writing code by hand.

sentences.en: What comes next, I'm not quite certain.
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么，我不太确定。

sentences.en: I want to talk about all this more.
sentences.zh: 我想多谈谈这一切。

sentences.en: I want to see how other developers are fairing.

content_html_zh:
10 Aug, 2026

我已经编程 20 年了。 它最初是作为青少年的一种爱好，制作粉丝网站和小视频游戏。 然后它变成了一种职业。 这是我非常喜欢做的事情。 我喜欢学习，我喜欢解决问题，我喜欢创造东西，这就是编程的很多内容。 在过去的 18 个月里，由于 LLM 驱动的编码工具（例如 Claude Code）和通常所说的“代理编程”的引入，我的职业生涯、我的爱好和我的手艺都发生了巨大的变化。 由于它对环境、社会和我的心理健康产生负面影响，我决定停止使用它。

▶ 观看本文的漫游视频版本。

几年前，我第一次意识到使用 LLM 进行编程是通过 GitHub 在 Visual Studio Code 中的 Copilot 集成，这就像类固醇的自动完成功能。 您开始输入函数 sortNames，它会向您显示该实现的预览。 我尝试了一下，发现它会分散注意力，而且基本上没什么用。 第二次出现是早期的聊天界面。 一位同事正在使用它来帮助调查问题，而法学硕士为他们提供的解决方案不起作用。 事实证明，法学硕士幻想了一个不存在的软件库版本，因此无法安装或使用来解决问题。

大约在这个时候，在那份工作中，一位真正的人工智能信徒被聘为产品团队的负责人。 他们是一名产品经理，开始使用法学硕士支持的编码工具提交更改，但不了解对更广泛系统的影响。 讨论的焦点变成了如何将人工智能集成到客户使用的软件中。 我看着它像病毒一样在整个组织中传播，而我则像几十年前一样继续编程，编写测试和构建功能，并在很大程度上享受这项工作。

在我写这篇文章时的一份新工作中，我继续编写我的整个生活。 编写TypeScript、Ruby、CSS等以及相应的测试，与其他系统和依赖项集成。 这是一个不到 10 名开发人员的小团队。 在协作通话中，我会看到我的一些同事如何在光标编辑器中利用人工智能，快速完成代码，有时提示它内联编写一些代码。 当时由法学硕士支持的编码工具主要是在本地到该文件的小范围内工作。 我认为它很简洁，几乎神奇，但没有什么能让我远离 Neovim 和 tmux，而且我觉得无论如何我的工作速度都足够快。

我过去没有，现在仍然没有看到加快工作速度的必要性。 我真的很喜欢卡尔·纽波特在他的《慢速生产力》一书中所鼓励的内容：以自然的节奏工作。

2025 年初，管理层问我一个问题：“你觉得人工智能编码的东西怎么样？” 我说“它经常是错误的，妨碍我，并且不能帮助我更快地编码，所以我不使用它。” 管理层在参加一次会议后不久就会相信法学硕士将如何改变我们对知识工作的了解，彻底改变工作场所。 这导致了使用人工智能工具的强制要求，否则就会被抛在后面。

我决定认真地尝试一下人工智能。 我尝试了光标编辑器，但它不适合我，并且在 Linux 上运行得很糟糕。 所以我尝试了 Zed，不久之后我就利用带有自动编辑功能的侧边栏聊天让法学硕士更改代码并构建软件。 当时真的感觉很神奇。 在一个框中输入内容，它就会编写代码并回答我的问题。 2025 年中期，代理编辑成为使用 AI 进行编码的新方式，取代了基于自动完成的工作流程。 随着人工智能公司投资为此目的调整的培训模型并构建编码工具，其功能不断变得越来越好。

快进一年到 2026 年中期。 在我决定停止使用人工智能之前，我基本上能够将 Linear 与 Claude Code 连接起来，并让它从头到尾构建一个不平凡的项目，而无需我编辑一行代码。 这项工作完成得比我自己更快。 我几乎不需要思考。 如果你是一个从完成更多工作中获益的人，这听起来很神奇，但这样做也有巨大的缺点，我稍后会详细分享。 我分享这个轶事是为了说：我了解基于 LLM 的编码工具的能力。 我是从一位经验丰富的首席工程师的角度写下这一切的，他认真使用了这些工具一年多了。 我不能再有意识地继续使用人工智能进行编码（或其他任何事情）。

在我开始使用LLM编码工具的同时，我也开始使用聊天功能。 我会要求它给我推荐书籍。 我会寻求职业建议。 我会通过它来表达商业想法。 我像朋友一样和它交谈。 我提出了宏伟的想法，并且总是得到支持。 我会向它寻求医疗建议。 我不好意思承认这一点，但有一天晚上，当我生病时，我描述了我所有的症状，它告诉我去医院的急诊室。 于是我在半夜跳上车，患上了流感，开车去了急诊室。 我坐在候诊室里等了两个小时，离开前服用的布洛芬开始发挥作用。 当我去看医生时，他们基本上只是告诉我回家休息，不需要去急诊室。 当然，是的，安全总比后悔有时适用于急诊室，但我认为依靠人工智能聊天来针对我的医疗状况采取什么行动是一个巨大的错误。 我也花了几百美元。 这个例子让我意识到人工智能聊天让我产生了妄想。

我停止使用人工智能聊天，因为很明显它没有帮助或不健康，而且实际上很危险。 但我在工作中一直使用人工智能进行编码，用它来承担越来越多的繁重工作，以至于我只是一名代码审查员和编码工具所吐出的功能的质量保证测试员。 完成很多任务，会让人感到兴奋。 也就是说，直到我意识到，好吧，我基本上只是一只轮子上的仓鼠，检查箱子，毫无意义地完成门票。 当然，我在这里或那里发现了一个问题。 但不可能审查人工智能编写的代码数量，而且无论如何我们都有不同的人工智能来审查它！ 那么这是做什么的呢？ 嗯，这让我变得懒惰了。 这让我不再关心。 这让我成为了一个更糟糕的程序员。 这让我很沮丧。 因为我停止了艰苦的工作，我停止了学习，我停止了成长，我不再是软件的制作者。

我与管理层进行了一次对话，讨论开发人员现在的工作是教人工智能变得更好，减少错误等等。审查代码。 并测试人工智能所做的改变。 这是一种可怕的存在，这是我无法继续这样下去的其他迹象之一。

必须做出改变的其他迹象之一是，我在工作中使用人工智能进行编码的次数越多，我对软件及其功能的感觉就越遥远。 如果不询问人工智能，我就无法准确解释某些东西是如何工作的。 我不太关心代码和软件本身，因为我自己没有编写任何代码，我被从其中删除了。

经过反思，我开始相信，高质量的软件并不在于某个东西有多少功能或者它的构建速度有多快，而是在于设计者、开发者和产品人员对其工作的关心程度。 我最喜欢的软件有一个难以形容的方面，我不认为它是一个功能矩阵，而是一个由人类为人类制作的界面，使用起来很有趣。 当你用人工智能构建软件时，它会导致更糟糕的软件。 当然，最初构建速度更快，但我认为这会损害代码质量、用户界面和用户体验。

我也开始经历存在主义的恐惧。 如果我基本上只是将 Linear 票证输入 CLI，那为什么还需要我呢？ 几年后软件工程还会存在吗？ 我应该成为一名电工还是其他职业？ 但我所热爱的这门手艺和我所拥有的职业又如何呢？ 它会消失吗？

我开始更多地了解人工智能的真正成本，从数据中心到用水等等。 它是在窃取的资源上构建和训练的。 而且成本是极端的。 除非他们在您的后院建立数据中心（在您意识到之前他们可能就在您的后院），否则这种成本在很大程度上是对人们隐藏的。

总而言之：使用人工智能进行编码会导致抑郁、冷漠、生存恐惧和更糟糕的软件。 不好。 再加上人工智能对环境、社区和经济的负面影响，对我来说，很明显有些事情必须改变。

今年早些时候，在这一切的最低谷时，我又回到了我的爱好之一：游戏编程。 这段时间，我为 Playdate 写完了关于游戏编码的书，制作了一些小游戏，并用 Rust 创建了一个名为 Usagi 的 2D Lua 游戏引擎。 我对工作中的编码感到幻灭，在没有人工智能的情况下通过编写和编码回到基础知识帮助我意识到我有多么喜欢编码以及使用人工智能如何使我成为一个更糟糕的程序员并对我的精神状态产生负面影响。

我尝试在工作中减少人工智能的使用，比如只将其用于琐碎的任务，但这从未真正奏效。 我会重新使用它来完成几乎所有事情。 当你可以让人工智能完成所有的事情时，编写一个测试感觉很愚蠢。 对我来说，这感觉像是一个全有或全无的决定。 此外，减少使用它但仍然使用它意味着我仍然会使用它，因此显示出对它的需求并加剧了它造成的危害。 不，谢谢。

当有人决定使用某种技术，或者更抽象地说是一种工具时，使用它总是会产生某种成本。 在我看来，使用基于法学硕士的工具的成本太高，对于我自己或社会来说绝对不值得。 在我看来，与人工智能可能提供的任何好处相比，人工智能无疑是一种净危害。

简而言之：我不喜欢这个人们使用人工智能来生成艺术、音乐、写作和软件的世界。 所以我不会使用AI。

我不知道停止在工作中使用人工智能进行编码的决定会产生什么后果。 我可能会被解雇。 或许我能过得很好。 时间会证明一切。 但我只知道我不能继续这样工作，因为这无疑会毁掉我的生活。

接下来会发生什么，我不太确定。 我想多谈谈这一切。 我想看看其他开发者是如何应对的。 我想回到我对分享我所学到的东西并通过写作和视频帮助其他程序员的热爱。 嗯，帮助那些真正想要学习编程的人，而不是那些只想提示他们找到解决方案的人。 这是一个奇怪且不确定的时期，这是肯定的。 但我会看看未来会发生什么，并坚持我的价值观并忠于自己。 这里是手动编写代码。
